# COR022 `missing-default-pointer-initialisation`

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="enabled by default" />

A pointer component of a derived type has no default initialisation (`=> null()`).

## Why

A pointer component without default initialisation starts with an *undefined* association status,
not a disassociated one: `associated(obj%p)` on a fresh object is not allowed and returns garbage
in practice, so code that tests it before use crashes or follows a wild pointer. `=> null()` in
the component declaration makes every new object start disassociated.

## Reported

```fortran
type :: node
  type(node), pointer :: next
end type node
```

## Preferred

```fortran
type :: node
  type(node), pointer :: next => null()
end type node
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[COR022] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = COR022` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/fobos/lint).

## Equivalent

Fortitude rule `C101` (see [Lint Rules](/lint-rules/#relation-to-fortitude)).
